health_canada_integration.approach: The portal NEVER connects directly to a Health Canada endpoint — there is no canada.ca AS2 URL. Health Canada's CESG rides on the US FDA Electronic Submissions Gateway (ESG). Onboarding: (1) obtain an X.509 certificate from a recognized CA; (2) create an FDA ESG account (WebTrader for manual upload or AS2/EDIINT for system-to-system); (3) complete the mandatory Test-gateway round-trip (must receive acknowledgements) before Production is granted; (4) designate 'HC' as the recipient Center so the FDA gateway auto-forwards to Health Canada. Identifiers are acquired up front through the Regulatory Enrolment Process (REP, mandatory since Oct 2020): the CO template emits the 5-digit Company ID and contact IDs; a product-type-branched Dossier ID request (validated to ^m[0-9]{6}$ for drugs) is filed ≥8 weeks before the first transaction; an RT template XML accompanies every transaction and a PI template where required — all REP XML filenames are template-generated and immutable and must be carried verbatim. Packaging assembles <dossierId>/<NNNN>/m1/ca/ca-regional.xml + m2–m5 + util/, generates the ICH index.xml and index-md5.txt, writes the Canadian Module 1 backbone (Schema v2.2, <hcsc_ectd>/<m1-administrative-and-product-information>), computes and re-verifies per-leaf MD5 (checksum-type 'MD5'), and assigns lifecycle operations (new/replace/append/delete) with valid prior-leaf back-references. A local validator mirroring HC Validation Rules v5.3 runs as a hard gate (block on any Error, advise on Warnings), enforcing 4-digit no-gap sequencing (A05a/A05b/A07), no empty folders (A01), file ≤200 MB (A03), path ≤200 chars (B08), valid/single backbone (A06a/H08), no encrypted/corrupt files (A09), and searchable PDFs (B49/D29). Transmission enforces the 10 GB per-transaction ceiling (>10 GB routes to physical media), the after-16:30-EST option for 5–10 GB, and one-transaction-at-a-time-per-dossier (wait for ACK before sending the next sequence). A delivery state machine consumes the three-stage acknowledgement chain — MDN (transport receipt) → FDA Acknowledgement/ACK1 → Health Canada Acknowledgement Receipt/ACK2 — and only treats a transaction as received by Health Canada on the HC Acknowledgement Receipt; the emailed eCTD Validation Report PDF is ingested and mapped back to the tree on rejection. Post-receipt, the portal models the DSTS lifecycle (processing → screening with SAL/SDN/SRL → review with clarifax clock-stops → NOC/NOD/NON, with withdrawal/reconsideration). The backbone generator sits behind an interface so the same content model can later emit the eCTD v4.0 HL7-RPS message (UUIDs, Genericode controlled vocabularies, Context of Use, two-way messaging) for the ~2028 mandate.

Acknowledgement-ingestion subsystem parsing MDN/AS2-MDN, FDA ACK1, and the Health Canada Acknowledgement Receipt, plus the emailed eCTD Validation Report PDF

differentiators: Validation-first by construction: HC Validation Rules v5.3 run continuously inline during authoring (not as a terminal gate), each defect mapped to the exact file/node with a one-click fix — versus incumbents where broken links, M1 metadata gaps, and checksum/naming errors surface only at the end and force costly republish cycles

ANDS-native intelligence: the only portal that branches on submission type to actively suppress Module 4 and the CS-BE-replaced Modules 2.4–2.7, validates pharmaceutical equivalence to the CRP, and validates AUC/Cmax 90% CIs against the 80.00–125.00% limits — generic-specific guidance baked in, not a generic publisher repurposed

Lifecycle clarity: a visual 'current view' reconstruction across sequences with enforced valid prior-leaf references for every replace/append/delete, eliminating the fragile, rework-prone multi-sequence tracking that plagues docuBridge/EXTEDO-class tools

Truthful, closed-loop transmission: the only tool that models CESG correctly as FDA-ESG-routed (no fake direct-HC endpoint), shows 'received by Health Canada' only on the HC Acknowledgement Receipt (not the MDN), and ingests the emailed validation report straight back onto the tree

Unified single-entry metadata: REP CO/RT/PI identifiers entered once flow into both the REP XML and the eCTD backbone, killing the re-keying that comes from disconnected authoring/publishing/RIM/validation systems

v4.0-ready without re-platforming: persistent document UUIDs and a version-pluggable backbone abstraction mean the same content emits v3.2.2 now and the HL7-RPS v4.0 message (Genericode vocabularies, Context of Use, two-way messaging) for the ~2028 mandate — answering the readiness uncertainty incumbents leave open

Low-friction, accessible delivery: a guided web UI with automated bookmarking/hyperlinking and zero scripting, priced for small/mid sponsors that today's high-TCO, training-heavy desktop publishers price out

Built-in Canadian compliance spine: Protected B in-Canada residency, an always-on tamper-evident audit trail no admin can disable, ALCOA+ e-signatures, and PIPEDA breach management shipped as core — not bolted-on services

Regulatory-clock intelligence: a DSTS-equivalent deadline engine that tracks ANDS 180-day review and SDN/clarifax/NOD windows with clock-stops, auto-flags at-risk filings against the 90%-on-time standard, and turns deadline lapses (which HC auto-interprets as withdrawal) into proactive reminders and pre-built Q&A response sequences

functional.statement: WHEN a sponsor org begins onboarding, the system SHALL provide a Company (CO) template form that captures sponsor details and emits a conformant REP CO XML file whose template-generated filename (pattern final-com-<COMPANYID>-<YYYY-MM-DD>-<HHMM>.xml) is preserved verbatim and never editable by any user.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a completed CO form WHEN the user generates the CO XML THEN the system produces a 'final-' prefixed XML file and records the returned 5-digit Company ID against the org
GIVEN a generated REP CO XML WHEN any user attempts to rename or change its extension THEN the system blocks the action and warns that REP filenames are immutable
GIVEN a CO form WHEN the user adds a contact and saves THEN the system stores the contact and its HC-issued contact ID for reference by later transactions
functional.rationale: REP CO is the mandatory front-door identifier acquisition; HC-generated immutable filenames must be carried verbatim or the transaction is rejected.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH REP topic: 'FILE NAMING IS MACHINE-GENERATED AND IMMUTABLE' + Company ID 5-digit; VISION Onboarding & Enrolment Wizard

functional.statement: WHEN a user requests a Dossier ID, the system SHALL provide a product-type-branched request workflow (human drug/biologic, veterinary, biocide, medical device) that enforces an 8-week lead-time gate before the intended first-filing date and tracks request status until the HC-assigned ID is returned.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a Dossier ID request WHEN the user selects a product type THEN the system presents the corresponding HC request form fields and lead-time guidance
GIVEN an intended first-filing date less than 8 weeks away WHEN the user submits the request THEN the system flags the lead-time violation and warns the dossier may not be ready in time
GIVEN a returned Dossier ID for a drug WHEN it is entered THEN the system validates it against ^m[0-9]{6}$ and rejects non-conforming values
functional.rationale: A valid Dossier ID is a hard prerequisite to assembling any transaction; the ~8-week HC lead time must be modelled in the workflow.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH REP topic: Dossier ID m+6 digits, 8-week lead; VISION Onboarding & Enrolment Wizard

functional.statement: WHEN a sponsor configures transmission, the system SHALL capture FDA ESG account setup (WebTrader or AS2/EDIINT), allow X.509 certificate upload, designate 'HC' as the recipient Center, and require a successful Test-gateway round-trip (acknowledgements received) before any Production transmission is permitted.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN no completed Test-gateway round-trip WHEN a user attempts a Production transmission THEN the system blocks it and directs the user to complete the test checklist
GIVEN ESG setup WHEN the user selects AS2 vs WebTrader THEN the system stores the account type and required certificate/config as first-class data
GIVEN a transmission configuration WHEN saved THEN the recipient Center is set to 'HC' and the system never targets a direct Health Canada AS2 endpoint
functional.rationale: CESG rides on the FDA ESG; a successful test round-trip is mandated before production and there is no direct HC endpoint.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH CESG topic: ONBOARDING steps, no direct HC endpoint, Test before Production; VISION health_canada_integration

functional.statement: WHEN a new submission is created, the system SHALL present a submission-type router (NDS/ANDS/SNDS/SANDS/DIN) with decision support and, when ANDS is selected, configure the ANDS content model so Module 4 is marked not-required and the CS-BE path suppresses Modules 2.4-2.7.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN ANDS is selected WHEN the content model is configured THEN Module 4 is shown as not-required and Module 3 (CMC) and Module 5 BE reports are shown as required
GIVEN the CS-BE path is toggled on WHEN the tree is rendered THEN Modules 2.4-2.7 are suppressed and the 2.3 QOS remains required
GIVEN a generic seeking a new indication beyond the CRP WHEN routing THEN the system advises that ANDS is generally not the correct pathway
functional.rationale: ANDS-native module gating prevents wrong-module effort and missing-content rejections; it is the core differentiator vs a generic publisher.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH ANDS topic: Module 4 not required, CS-BE replaces 2.4-2.7; VISION New Submission Intake & Type Router

functional.statement: WHEN an ANDS submission is configured, the system SHALL resolve the regulatory activity type from a controlled vocabulary that includes ANDS and feed it into the REP RT template, rejecting any value not in HC's controlled vocabulary.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN activity-type selection WHEN the user picks a value THEN only HC controlled-vocabulary values are selectable
GIVEN a resolved activity type WHEN an RT template is generated THEN the activity type and regulatory activity lead populate the RT XML
GIVEN a metadata value not in the controlled vocabulary WHEN validation runs THEN the system raises an Error mirroring rule I08
functional.rationale: Activity/enumeration values not in HC controlled vocabulary cause rejection (I08); RT must accompany every transaction.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH eCTD topic rule I08; REP topic RT template; VISION New Submission Intake & Type Router

functional.statement: The system SHALL generate a Regulatory Transaction (RT) template XML for every regulatory transaction, and a Product Information (PI) template where the transaction subset requires it, preserving template-generated immutable filenames and placing them in Module 1.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN any transaction WHEN it is assembled THEN an RT XML is generated and placed in Module 1
GIVEN a transaction subset requiring PI WHEN assembled THEN a PI template XML is also generated; otherwise PI is omitted
GIVEN generated RT/PI XML WHEN packaged THEN their HC-template filenames are carried verbatim
functional.rationale: RT is mandatory with every transaction and PI for a subset; both must be conformant and immutably named.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH REP topic: RT mandatory each transaction, PI subset; VISION REP integration feature

functional.statement: WHEN capturing the Canadian Reference Product, the system SHALL require structured CRP fields (brand name, DIN, strength, dosage form, innovator/manufacturer) and provide a foreign-CRP justification path, validating that the proposed generic is pharmaceutically equivalent (identical medicinal ingredient(s) in comparable dosage form).
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a CRP entry WHEN required fields are missing THEN the system blocks progression and lists the missing fields
GIVEN a proposed generic and CRP WHEN medicinal ingredient or dosage-form comparability fails THEN the system flags a pharmaceutical-equivalence defect
GIVEN a foreign-sourced reference product WHEN selected THEN the system requires a justification record per the foreign-CRP path
functional.rationale: The CRP and pharmaceutical equivalence are the legal heart of an ANDS (C.08.001.1 / C.08.002.1).
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH ANDS topic: CRP definition, pharmaceutical equivalence; VISION CRP & Bioequivalence Builder

functional.statement: WHEN building bioequivalence evidence, the system SHALL provide a CS-BE builder that outputs the 2.7.1 summary, links pivotal study reports into Module 5.3.1.2, and captures AUC/Cmax 90% confidence intervals validated against acceptance limits (AUC 80.00-125.00%; Cmax per guidance).
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN entered AUC 90% CI bounds WHEN they fall outside 80.00-125.00% THEN the system flags a bioequivalence acceptance-limit failure
GIVEN a completed CS-BE WHEN saved THEN it produces the 2.7.1 summary and creates leaf links to reports in 5.3.1.2
GIVEN Cmax CI values WHEN validated THEN the system checks them against the Cmax limits configured per guidance
functional.rationale: BE demonstration via AUC/Cmax 90% CI against the 80.00-125.00% limits and CS-BE placement in 2.7.1/5.3.1.2 is generic-specific intelligence incumbents lack.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH ANDS topic: BE, CS-BE, 5.3.1.2, AUC limits; VISION CRP & Bioequivalence Builder

functional.statement: The system SHALL drive the eCTD tree and Module 1 leaf placement from Health Canada's 'Organization and document placement' heading table (updated 2024-04-02) as versioned data, including required .docx-alongside-PDF documents where specified.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN the document-placement table WHEN the tree is rendered THEN each CA Module 1 heading maps to its prescribed leaf location
GIVEN a section that requires a .docx alongside the PDF WHEN the checklist renders THEN both formats are required for that section
GIVEN an updated placement table WHEN loaded THEN placement changes apply without code changes
functional.rationale: Driving placement from HC's heading table as data (not hardcoded) keeps the portal current and prevents misplacement rejections.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH eCTD topic: HC heading reference table 2024-04-02; VISION Dossier Workspace / CTD Tree Editor

functional.statement: WHEN documents are uploaded into the workspace, the system SHALL enforce PDF conformance (versions 1.4-1.7, text-based/searchable with OCR for scanned pages, fonts embedded, no encryption/passwords/security settings, no enabled Track Changes, not corrupt).
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN an encrypted or password-protected PDF WHEN uploaded THEN the system blocks it with an Error mirroring rule A09
GIVEN a scanned non-searchable PDF WHEN uploaded THEN the system flags it for OCR mirroring rules B49/D29
GIVEN a PDF outside versions 1.4-1.7 or with Track Changes enabled WHEN validated THEN the system raises a conformance defect mapped to the file
functional.rationale: Non-searchable, secured, or corrupt PDFs are common rejection triggers (A09/B49/D29) and must be caught before packaging.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH eCTD topic PDF rules A09/B49/D29; VISION Dossier Workspace / CTD Tree Editor

functional.statement: WHEN a PDF exceeding 10 pages is uploaded, the system SHALL automatically generate single-action bookmarks (one action per bookmark opening its destination), with the documented exceptions for literature references in 3.3/4.3/5.4 and Health Canada e-forms.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN an 11-page content PDF WHEN uploaded THEN the system generates bookmarks and each bookmark has exactly one action
GIVEN a literature reference under 3.3/4.3/5.4 or an HC e-form WHEN uploaded THEN bookmark generation is exempted
GIVEN generated bookmarks WHEN validation runs THEN no broken/multi-action bookmark defects are raised
functional.rationale: Manual bookmarking is one of the most error-prone, time-consuming RA tasks; automating it is a major pass-rate and productivity win.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH tool-landscape topic: bookmarks >10 pages, single action, 3.3/4.3/5.4 + e-form exceptions; VISION automated PDF remediation feature

functional.statement: The system SHALL provide intra-document and inter-document hyperlinking that produces functional relative internal links and SHALL reject or flag external/absolute web hyperlinks in content PDFs.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a cross-reference within or between documents WHEN authored THEN the system creates a relative, functional hyperlink
GIVEN an absolute external web hyperlink in a content PDF WHEN validated THEN the system flags it as a defect mapped to the link
GIVEN a broken bookmark or hyperlink WHEN validation runs THEN the defect is surfaced before export
functional.rationale: Broken/external links are flagged by HC validation; automated relative linking removes a major manual error source.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH eCTD topic: relative internal links, no external hyperlinks; VISION automated PDF remediation feature

functional.statement: WHEN a content file approaches or exceeds the per-file size limit, the system SHALL warn at the 150-200 MB band and hard-block any single PDF at or above 200 MB (mirroring A03a/A03b), offering an automated oversize-split workflow.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a 170 MB PDF WHEN validated THEN the system issues a non-blocking Warning advising a split
GIVEN a 210 MB PDF WHEN validated THEN the system raises a blocking Error and offers to split the file
GIVEN a non-PDF file above the configured non-PDF ceiling WHEN validated THEN the system raises the corresponding Error
functional.rationale: Files >=200 MB error in HC validation; pre-empting and auto-splitting prevents republish cycles.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH CESG topic: 200 MB PDF Error, 150-200 MB Warning; VISION Pre-Submission Validation Report

functional.statement: The system SHALL deterministically generate both backbones for each sequence — the ICH index.xml with index-md5.txt at the sequence root, and the Canadian ca-regional.xml under m1/ca/ conformant to Canadian Module 1 Schema v2.2 — plus the util/ folder, validating each against its schema/DTD before export.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a sequence WHEN backbones are generated THEN index.xml, index-md5.txt and m1/ca/ca-regional.xml exist with root <hcsc_ectd> and <m1-administrative-and-product-information>
GIVEN a generated backbone WHEN it fails schema/DTD validation THEN the system blocks export with an Error mirroring A06a/H08
GIVEN two backbone generation runs on identical content WHEN compared THEN the output is byte-deterministic
functional.rationale: Backbone/schema errors (A06a, H08) are top rejection triggers; dual-backbone correctness is non-negotiable for acceptance.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH eCTD topic: index.xml + index-md5.txt + ca-regional.xml Schema v2.2; VISION dual-backbone generator feature

functional.statement: WHEN a sequence is saved or exported, the system SHALL compute a per-leaf MD5 checksum (checksum-type 'MD5'), record it in the backbone, write index-md5.txt for index.xml, and re-verify every stored checksum against the actual file bytes, hard-blocking on any mismatch.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN leaf files WHEN a sequence is saved THEN each leaf carries a matching MD5 and checksum-type attribute
GIVEN a file altered after checksum computation WHEN re-verification runs THEN the system raises a blocking checksum-mismatch Error
GIVEN index.xml WHEN written THEN index-md5.txt contains its correct MD5 hash
functional.rationale: Checksum mismatch or missing index-md5.txt is an Error and a top rejection trigger; re-verification against bytes is mandatory.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH eCTD topic: MD5 per leaf, index-md5.txt, mismatch = Error; VISION dual-backbone generator feature

functional.statement: The system SHALL auto-assign 4-digit zero-padded sequence numbers per dossier (initial = 0000, strictly +1 with no gaps and no repeats) and block any transaction that would skip, repeat, or precede a missing predecessor (mirroring A05a/A05b/A07).
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a new dossier's first transaction WHEN created THEN the sequence folder is exactly 0000
GIVEN existing sequences 0000 and 0001 WHEN the next is created THEN it is assigned 0002 and no gap is allowed
GIVEN an attempt to file 0004 while 0003 is missing WHEN validated THEN the system blocks with an Error mirroring A05b/A07
functional.rationale: Gapped/out-of-order sequencing (A05/A07) causes rejection; server-side enforcement removes a dominant incumbent failure mode.

functional.statement: WHEN a user replaces, appends, or deletes a leaf, the system SHALL require and persist a valid reference to a prior leaf that exists in the current or a prior sequence, preventing any dangling cross-reference in the emitted backbone.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a replace operation WHEN no valid prior leaf is referenced THEN the system blocks the operation and flags a dangling-reference defect
GIVEN a delete operation on a leaf originally added as 'new' WHEN applied THEN the backbone points to the correct prior leaf ID
GIVEN all operations across sequences WHEN backbone is emitted THEN no leaf operation references a non-existent prior leaf
functional.rationale: A replace/append/delete with a dangling reference is a validation Error; correct lifecycle linkage is a core correctness requirement.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH lifecycle topic: leaf operations + prior-leaf reference; VISION Lifecycle & Sequence Manager

functional.statement: The system SHALL reconstruct and display the 'current view' of a dossier — the set of leaves that are live after applying all new/replace/append/delete operations across all sequences — and SHALL use it to validate that delete/replace targets exist.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN multiple sequences with lifecycle operations WHEN the current view is requested THEN only live leaves are shown with their originating sequence
GIVEN a replaced leaf WHEN current view renders THEN the superseded leaf is excluded from the live set but retained in history
GIVEN a delete targeting a leaf not in the current view WHEN validated THEN the system raises a defect
functional.rationale: Visual current-view reconstruction eliminates the fragile, rework-prone multi-sequence tracking that plagues incumbent tools.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH lifecycle topic: current-view reconstruction; VISION Lifecycle clarity differentiator

functional.statement: The system SHALL support file reuse, allowing a later sequence to re-point to an unchanged physical file from an earlier sequence rather than re-shipping the bytes, while preserving correct checksums and references.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN an unchanged document WHEN a new sequence reuses it THEN the backbone re-points to the prior physical file without duplicating bytes
GIVEN a reused file WHEN packaged THEN the recorded checksum still matches the referenced file
GIVEN a reused file later replaced WHEN validated THEN the replace correctly references the reused leaf
functional.rationale: File reuse reduces package size and matches eCTD lifecycle semantics; helps stay under transmission ceilings.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH lifecycle topic: file reuse; VISION Lifecycle & Sequence Manager

functional.statement: The system SHALL enforce file/folder naming and path hygiene before packaging: lowercase a-z, digits and hyphens only, no spaces or accented/non-ASCII characters, no reserved Windows names, unique leaf IDs, and total path length within 200 characters from the sequence root (mirroring B08, B32, B47/B48).
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a filename with spaces or non-ASCII characters WHEN validated THEN the system raises a naming Error and proposes a compliant name
GIVEN a leaf path exceeding 200 characters WHEN validated THEN the system raises a blocking Error mirroring B08
GIVEN duplicate leaf titles in Modules 2-5 or duplicate leaf IDs WHEN validated THEN the system raises the corresponding defect
functional.rationale: Path-length overflow and naming/leaf-ID violations are common rejection triggers (B08/B32/B47/B48).
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH eCTD topic: naming rules, B08, B32, B47/B48; VISION Pre-Submission Validation Report

functional.statement: The system SHALL block packaging of any sequence that contains an empty folder (mirroring A01).
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a sequence containing an empty module/sub folder WHEN validated THEN the system raises a blocking Error mirroring A01
GIVEN all folders contain at least one leaf or required file WHEN validated THEN the empty-folder check passes
GIVEN an empty folder defect WHEN displayed THEN it is mapped to the exact folder path
functional.rationale: Empty folders (A01) are a frequent rejection trigger and must be caught before transmission.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH eCTD topic A01; VISION Pre-Submission Validation Report

functional.statement: The system SHALL run a versioned validation-rules engine (default v5.3, effective 2025-05-31; active version selectable) that models each rule as {rule_id, category, severity, description, ruleset_version} across the General/PDF/Referenced/XML/ICH-Backbone/Regional/STF/REP categories, blocking on any Error and surfacing Warnings non-blocking.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN the active ruleset is v5.3 WHEN validation runs THEN findings carry rule IDs, category and severity from that version
GIVEN a selectable prior ruleset version WHEN chosen THEN validation evaluates against that version's rules without code changes
GIVEN any Error-severity finding WHEN present THEN transmission is blocked; GIVEN only Warnings THEN transmission is allowed with advisories
functional.rationale: HC updates the ruleset ~annually; a data-driven, versioned engine delivers 'first-pass-clean by construction' without redeploys.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH eCTD topic: versioned ruleset v5.3, categories, two-tier severity; VISION continuous validation engine feature

functional.statement: The system SHALL run the validation rules continuously (inline) during authoring, presenting each defect in a severity-colored gutter mapped to the exact file/node with a one-click fix where remediable, rather than only as a terminal gate.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a defect introduced during authoring WHEN it occurs THEN it appears inline mapped to the exact file/node within the editing session
GIVEN a remediable defect WHEN the user clicks the one-click fix THEN the system applies the correction and re-validates
GIVEN Error vs Warning findings WHEN displayed THEN Errors are shown as blocking and Warnings as advisory by color
functional.rationale: Late, terminal validation feedback is the #1 RA pain point; continuous inline validation with one-click fixes is the lead differentiator.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH tool-landscape topic: late validation pain point; VISION continuous validation engine differentiator

functional.statement: The system SHALL produce a downloadable pre-submission validation report that mirrors HC's output — a categorized Error/Warning list with rule IDs against the pinned ruleset version, plus a backbone preview (rendered index.xml and ca-regional.xml) with each leaf's MD5 verified against actual bytes.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a built sequence WHEN the report is generated THEN it lists findings grouped by category with rule IDs and severities
GIVEN the report WHEN viewed THEN it renders index.xml and ca-regional.xml previews with per-leaf verified MD5 status
GIVEN any unresolved Error WHEN the report is generated THEN it marks the transaction as not transmittable
functional.rationale: Mirroring HC's validation output so nothing reaches CESG that HC will reject is the validation-first thesis.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH eCTD topic: pre-submission report mirroring HC; VISION Pre-Submission Validation Report

functional.statement: WHEN a transaction is ready to transmit, the system SHALL enforce the 10 GB per-transaction ceiling pre-flight: packages at or below 10 GB route to the FDA ESG gateway; packages above 10 GB are blocked from the gateway and routed to the physical-media (USB/HDD) workflow with shipping instructions.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a 6 GB package WHEN transmission is requested THEN the gateway path is available
GIVEN a 12 GB package WHEN transmission is requested THEN the gateway path is blocked and the physical-media workflow is presented
GIVEN the physical-media workflow WHEN selected THEN the system surfaces shipping/media instructions
functional.rationale: 10 GB is the hard CESG ceiling; over-limit transactions cannot go through the gateway and must use physical media.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH CESG topic: 10 GB ceiling, >10 GB physical media; VISION Transmission Console

functional.statement: WHEN a package is between 5 GB and 10 GB, the system SHALL offer to schedule transmission after 16:30 EST per Health Canada congestion guidance.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a 7 GB package WHEN transmission is requested THEN the system offers an after-16:30-EST scheduling option
GIVEN a scheduled send WHEN 16:30 EST is reached THEN the system transmits the queued transaction
GIVEN a sub-5 GB package WHEN transmission is requested THEN no after-16:30 scheduling prompt is required
functional.rationale: HC recommends sending 5-10 GB transactions after 16:30 EST to avoid gateway congestion.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH CESG topic: after-16:30-EST guidance; VISION Transmission Console

functional.statement: The system SHALL enforce one-transaction-at-a-time transmission per dossier, queueing any subsequent sequence until the Health Canada acknowledgement for the prior sequence has been received.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a sequence transmitted and awaiting acknowledgement WHEN the next sequence is queued THEN the system holds it until the prior acknowledgement arrives
GIVEN the prior sequence's HC acknowledgement is received WHEN the queue is processed THEN the next sequence becomes eligible to send
GIVEN two sequences for different dossiers WHEN transmitted THEN per-dossier serialization does not block the unrelated dossier
functional.rationale: CESG requires waiting for acknowledgement of one transaction before sending the next sequence for the same dossier.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH compliance topic: one-at-a-time sequencing per dossier; VISION Transmission Console

functional.statement: The system SHALL maintain an acknowledgement state machine (SENT -> MDN_RECEIVED -> FDA_ACK -> HC_ACK_RECEIPT) and SHALL display a transaction as 'received by Health Canada' only upon the Health Canada Acknowledgement Receipt, never on the MDN alone.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a transmitted transaction WHEN only the MDN is received THEN the UI shows transport receipt but not 'received by Health Canada'
GIVEN the FDA ACK1 is received WHEN displayed THEN the state advances to FDA_ACK without claiming HC receipt
GIVEN the Health Canada Acknowledgement Receipt is received WHEN displayed THEN the transaction is marked received by Health Canada
functional.rationale: Treating the MDN as success is a real correctness trap; only the HC Acknowledgement Receipt is true delivery.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH CESG topic: three-stage ack chain; VISION acknowledgement state machine feature

functional.statement: WHEN a transaction is rejected, the system SHALL ingest the emailed eCTD Validation Report PDF and map each reported error back to the exact file/node in the dossier tree for correction in the next sequence.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a rejection validation report PDF WHEN ingested THEN each listed error is parsed with its rule ID
GIVEN parsed errors WHEN displayed THEN each maps to the corresponding file/node in the tree
GIVEN a corrected next sequence WHEN built THEN the previously reported errors are re-validated as resolved
functional.rationale: Ingesting the emailed validation report and mapping it back to the tree closes the rejection feedback loop.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH lifecycle topic: emailed eCTD Validation Report; VISION acknowledgement state machine feature

functional.statement: The system SHALL model the post-receipt DSTS lifecycle as a state machine: Processing (~10 days) -> Screening (45-day target, with SAL/SDN/SRL outcomes) -> Review (ANDS 180-day target) -> decision (NOC/NOD/NON), reflecting DSTS-equivalent statuses including Inactive 45 and Inactive 90.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a transaction received by HC WHEN tracking starts THEN the status begins at Processing and advances through the modelled phases
GIVEN an SDN is recorded WHEN the status updates THEN it transitions to Inactive 45
GIVEN a decision is recorded WHEN entered THEN the status reflects NOC, NOD, or NON

acceptance_criteria: GIVEN an SDN dated today WHEN the timer starts THEN a 45-day countdown with reminders is created
GIVEN a clarifax under the 180-300 day standard WHEN issued THEN a 15-day response window is set; under 0-90 day standard a 5-day window
GIVEN a NOD for an ANDS WHEN issued THEN a 90-day timer starts and the review clock is paused until response
functional.rationale: Deadline misses auto-convert to withdrawal; timers and clock-stops materially de-risk filings.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH fees/standards topic: clarifax tiers, SDN 45, NOD 90/45; VISION DSTS deadline engine feature

functional.statement: The system SHALL provide a Q&A-format response-sequence builder that attaches the original notice (SDN/clarifax/NOD/NON), authors answers referencing the applicable submission sections, and files the response as a new eCTD sequence in the same format as the original.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN an original notice WHEN a response is started THEN the builder attaches a copy of the notice to the new sequence
GIVEN a Q&A response WHEN authored THEN each answer references the applicable submission section
GIVEN a completed response WHEN filed THEN it becomes the next valid eCTD sequence in the same format
functional.rationale: Deficiency responses must be filed as new eCTD sequences in Q&A format including the original notice.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH lifecycle topic: Q&A response sequence; VISION DSTS Status Tracker

acceptance_criteria: GIVEN an SDN/NOD/NON response window that lapses WHEN the deadline passes THEN the system records an auto-interpreted withdrawal with the W status
GIVEN a withdrawn submission WHEN the sponsor refiles THEN the system allows refiling without blocking the dossier
GIVEN an NON/W WHEN the sponsor requests reconsideration THEN the system supports the reconsideration path
functional.rationale: HC auto-interprets deadline lapses as withdrawal; explicit modelling prevents surprise terminations and supports refiling/reconsideration.

GIVEN a dossier approaching its service-standard target WHEN evaluated THEN it is flagged at-risk
GIVEN the portfolio WHEN viewed THEN on-time performance is summarized against the 90% KPI

functional.statement: The system SHALL resolve an ANDS to its Schedule 1 fee grouping (typically 'Comparative studies'), compute the current fiscal-year amount via a CPI-escalation table keyed by April-1 effective date using Fee = A + (A x B), and display the grouping rationale, amount, and applicable fiscal year.

GIVEN a subsequent ANDS WHEN 50% remission is claimed THEN the system requires the affiliation/financial attestation upload
GIVEN a concurrent authorization application WHEN deferral is selected THEN payment is deferred until NOC and invoice status reflects deferral

GIVEN an approaching anniversary WHEN evaluated THEN the system schedules a reminder
GIVEN an unpaid annual fee WHEN reviewed THEN the DIN shows an outstanding-balance flag

GIVEN a QA audit-trail review WHEN completed THEN the named reviewer's sign-off is recorded

GIVEN an interrupted transmission (network drop mid-send) WHEN connectivity returns THEN the system resolves whether the transaction was received (via ack reconciliation) before allowing a duplicate send

GIVEN an MDN received but no FDA ACK within the configured window WHEN the monitor fires THEN the transaction is flagged for investigation and not auto-marked received

GIVEN an operator attempting to resend a sequence whose delivery state is unresolved WHEN resend is requested THEN the system requires explicit confirmation and records the duplicate-send rationale in the audit trail

functional.traces_to: GAP: explicit multi-dossier/multi-product/multi-DIN modeling and isolation absent

functional.statement: WHEN a sponsor needs to file an administrative or corrective sequence (e.g., a sequence that reorganizes, withdraws, or corrects a prior transaction's lifecycle without changing scientific content), the system SHALL support administrative-type regulatory activities and corrective/reorganization sequences that file as a valid next eCTD sequence with correct lifecycle operations and no scientific re-review trigger where not warranted.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a need to withdraw a single leaf erroneously filed WHEN a corrective sequence is built THEN the system files a delete operation referencing the correct prior leaf as the next sequence number
GIVEN an administrative regulatory activity type WHEN selected THEN the RT template and content model reflect the administrative subset, not a full ANDS content set
GIVEN a reorganization sequence WHEN assembled THEN the current-view reconstruction remains consistent and no dangling references are introduced
functional.rationale: Real dossiers require administrative and corrective sequences (correcting a mis-filed leaf, reorganizing); the existing model only contemplates content and deficiency-response sequences.
functional.traces_to: GAP: administrative/corrective/reorganization sequence types beyond REQ-032 deficiency responses

functional.statement: WHEN a sponsor must transfer ownership of a dossier/DIN to another company, change the company name, or merge/acquire another sponsor org, the system SHALL support a dossier/manufacturer transfer-of-ownership workflow that updates REP Company ID and contact records, preserves the full prior sequence history and audit trail, and files the appropriate administrative sequence.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a transfer of ownership WHEN executed THEN the dossier's full sequence history and audit trail are preserved and re-associated to the receiving org without rewriting prior sequences
GIVEN a company name change WHEN recorded THEN a new CO transaction is generated while prior Company ID linkage and history remain intact
GIVEN a transfer WHEN completed THEN tenant access is re-scoped so only the new owner org can access the dossier and the change is audit-logged with actor and timestamp
functional.rationale: Manufacturer transfers, name changes, and M&A are routine over a product lifecycle and touch REP identifiers, tenant isolation, and history preservation — none of which the current requirements address.
functional.traces_to: GAP: transfer-of-ownership / company name change / org merge lifecycle absent

functional.statement: WHEN a screening or review deficiency response is received from the sponsor that is incomplete, late, or itself deficient, the system SHALL distinguish among acceptable, deficient, and unsolicited responses, track the resulting HC outcome (e.g., acceptance, further clarifax, conversion to withdrawal), and prevent filing a response after the applicable window has closed without an explicit override and rationale.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a clarifax response prepared after its 5/10/15-day window has elapsed WHEN filing is attempted THEN the system warns the window has closed and requires an explicit override with recorded rationale
GIVEN a response HC deems deficient WHEN the outcome is recorded THEN the system advances the dossier state accordingly (e.g., to withdrawal interpretation) and timestamps it
GIVEN an unsolicited submission of additional data during review WHEN filed THEN the system tags it as unsolicited and records the regulatory risk advisory
functional.rationale: REQ-031/032/033 cover issuing timers and building responses but not the response-quality/late-response branch that actually triggers withdrawal or further clarifax — the core deficiency-workflow corner case.
functional.traces_to: GAP: deficient/late/unsolicited response handling beyond REQ-031/032/033

functional.statement: The system SHALL track multiple concurrent deficiency notices (e.g., overlapping clarifax requests, simultaneous screening and review queries) per dossier with independent clocks and clock-stops, and SHALL correctly recompute the review service-standard clock when overlapping sponsor response windows pause and resume it.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN two clarifax requests open simultaneously WHEN clocks run THEN each maintains its own response deadline and reminder schedule independently
GIVEN overlapping response windows WHEN the review clock-stop is computed THEN the system pauses the 180-day review clock for the union of active response windows and resumes correctly
GIVEN a closed clarifax while another remains open WHEN recomputed THEN the review clock reflects the still-paused state
functional.rationale: Real reviews have multiple overlapping clarifax cycles; a single clock-stop model (REQ-031) miscomputes the service standard when windows overlap, which directly affects withdrawal-risk and KPI accuracy.
functional.traces_to: GAP: concurrent/overlapping deficiency clocks and union clock-stop logic absent from REQ-031

functional.statement: The system SHALL compute and display the applicable regulatory deadlines using Health Canada's calendar conventions — calendar vs business days as specified per notice type, Canadian federal statutory holidays, and the configured review timezone — and SHALL not silently roll a deadline that lands on a weekend or holiday without surfacing the adjusted due date.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a 5-day clarifax window WHEN the nominal due date falls on a Canadian statutory holiday THEN the system shows the adjusted due date per HC convention and flags the adjustment
GIVEN a deadline computation WHEN calendar-day vs business-day basis differs by notice type THEN the system applies the correct basis for that notice type
GIVEN a holiday calendar update WHEN loaded as reference data THEN deadline computations reflect it without code changes
functional.rationale: Deadline misses auto-convert to withdrawal, so the exact day-counting basis, holidays, and timezone are material; the current timer requirements assume naive calendar math.
functional.traces_to: GAP: holiday/business-day/timezone-aware deadline computation absent from REQ-031/NFR-013

functional.statement: The system SHALL bind every applied electronic signature to an immutable signature manifest that records the exact artifact (sequence/leaf/backbone) and its checksum at signing time, the signer identity and authentication method, the signing timestamp with timezone, and the signature meaning, and SHALL detect and flag any post-signature modification of the signed content before transmission.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a transaction signed by an authorized signer WHEN the manifest is written THEN it records the signed artifact identifiers, their checksums at signing, signer identity, auth method, timestamp+timezone, and meaning
GIVEN content modified after signature WHEN the gate re-evaluates THEN the system invalidates the signature, flags the broken manifest, and re-blocks transmission
GIVEN a signed package WHEN exported THEN the signature manifest is retained and exportable as part of the audit record
functional.rationale: NFR-003/REQ-039 require e-signatures but not a tamper-evident signature-to-content manifest; an auditor demands proof that the signed bytes are the transmitted bytes and that post-signing edits invalidate the signature.
functional.traces_to: GAP: e-signature manifest binding signature to specific signed content + post-sign tamper detection, beyond NFR-003/REQ-039

functional.statement: The system SHALL enforce configurable data-retention and legal-hold policies on submission content, sequences, acknowledgements, audit trails, and signature manifests that meet or exceed Health Canada/PIPEDA minimum retention periods, prevent deletion of records under legal hold or within the retention window, and log any disposition event.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a record within its mandated retention window WHEN deletion is attempted THEN the system blocks it and records the blocked attempt
GIVEN a legal hold placed on a dossier WHEN any disposition is attempted THEN the system prevents it until the hold is released by an authorized role
GIVEN a record past retention with no hold WHEN disposition runs THEN the event is logged with actor, timestamp, and records affected
functional.rationale: Long-term retention and legal hold of regulatory records are standard audit/GxP demands; the current set covers breach-record retention (NFR-006) but not submission-record retention, legal hold, or controlled disposition.
functional.traces_to: GAP: retention schedule + legal hold + disposition logging absent

functional.statement: The system SHALL provide disaster-recovery and business-continuity capabilities for all dossier content, sequences, acknowledgements, audit trails, and signature manifests, including in-Canada backups, defined recovery point and recovery time objectives, and periodic tested restoration, without violating data-residency constraints.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a regional failure WHEN recovery is invoked THEN the system restores all dossier content, sequences, acks, audit trails, and signatures to within the defined RPO/RTO
GIVEN backups WHEN created THEN they remain pinned to in-Canada Protected B regions and are encrypted at rest
GIVEN a scheduled DR test WHEN executed THEN a documented restoration is performed and verified against integrity checksums
functional.rationale: NFR-010 mentions durability generally but defines no RPO/RTO, no tested restoration, and no residency-safe DR — all of which an auditor and a regulated SaaS contract require.
functional.traces_to: GAP: explicit DR/BCP with RPO/RTO, tested restore, residency-safe backups beyond NFR-010

functional.statement: WHEN HC's eCTD validation ruleset, Module 1 placement table, controlled vocabularies, or schema versions change while sequences are in flight, the system SHALL pin each transaction to the ruleset/schema version effective at its build/transmit time, prevent retroactive invalidation of already-accepted sequences, and warn when an in-progress dossier spans a version-effective-date boundary.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a sequence built under ruleset v5.3 WHEN a later ruleset becomes active THEN the accepted sequence's recorded validation result remains pinned to v5.3 and is not retroactively failed
GIVEN an in-progress draft WHEN a new ruleset effective date passes before transmission THEN the system warns and offers re-validation against the now-active version
GIVEN a schema version change WHEN a dossier's prior sequences used the older schema THEN the current-view and lifecycle references remain valid across the version boundary
functional.rationale: REQ-022/040/NFR-013 make rules data-driven but don't address version transitions mid-dossier — a real corner case where a long-running dossier crosses an effective-date boundary.
functional.traces_to: GAP: ruleset/schema version-transition pinning for in-flight dossiers beyond REQ-022/REQ-040

functional.statement: The system SHALL provide a concurrency/locking model for multi-user authoring of the same dossier and sequence that prevents conflicting simultaneous edits to leaves, metadata, lifecycle operations, and sequence numbering, and SHALL serialize sequence-number assignment so two users cannot both claim the same next 4-digit sequence.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN two users editing the same leaf concurrently WHEN both save THEN the system prevents a lost update via locking or conflict detection and surfaces the conflict
GIVEN two users creating the next sequence for the same dossier simultaneously WHEN they submit THEN exactly one obtains the next number and the other is rejected/retried
GIVEN a held lock WHEN the holder is idle beyond a timeout THEN the lock is safely released without corrupting state
functional.rationale: REQ-016 mandates gapless numbering but concurrent RA users could race the next-sequence assignment or clobber each other's leaf edits; without locking this corrupts the backbone.
functional.traces_to: GAP: multi-user concurrency/locking and serialized sequence assignment absent from REQ-016

functional.statement: WHEN a transaction is routed to the physical-media (>10 GB) workflow, the system SHALL produce a complete media package (the validated eCTD folder tree, backbones, checksums, and a media-manifest/cover documentation), track the physical shipment and its receipt, and reconcile the eventual Health Canada acknowledgement back to the same transaction record as the gateway path.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a >10 GB transaction WHEN the physical-media workflow runs THEN the system writes the full validated tree plus a media manifest and shipping documentation
GIVEN a shipped media package WHEN tracked THEN the system records carrier/tracking and receipt status against the transaction
GIVEN an HC acknowledgement for a media-shipped transaction WHEN received THEN it reconciles to the same dossier/sequence record and advances the DSTS lifecycle identically to gateway transactions
functional.rationale: REQ-025 routes >10 GB to physical media but stops at 'shipping instructions'; a real workflow must produce the media package, track the shipment, and close the acknowledgement loop.
functional.traces_to: GAP: physical-media package generation, shipment tracking, and ack reconciliation beyond REQ-025

functional.statement: The system SHALL validate cross-document and metadata consistency across a transaction — DIN/Dossier ID/Company ID agreement among CO/RT/PI, cover letter, and ca-regional.xml; product name, strength, and dosage-form consistency between CRP/PI metadata and content; and STF (Study Tagging File) presence and correctness where Module 4/5 study data requires it — blocking on inconsistencies before packaging.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN identifiers across CO/RT/PI, cover letter, and ca-regional.xml WHEN they disagree THEN the system blocks export and lists the conflicting values
GIVEN product/strength/dosage-form metadata WHEN inconsistent between PI/CRP and content placement THEN the system raises a consistency defect mapped to the source
GIVEN Module 5 study data that requires an STF WHEN the STF is missing or malformed THEN the system raises the corresponding STF-category defect
functional.rationale: The vision lists an STF validation category and single-entry metadata, but no requirement enforces cross-artifact metadata consistency or STF correctness — both are real HC validation/rejection triggers.
functional.traces_to: GAP: cross-artifact metadata-consistency and STF validation absent (STF category named in VISION ruleset, REQ-043 single-entry)

functional.statement: The system SHALL provide audit-trail export and regulatory-inspection support, producing on demand a complete, human-readable, time-ordered audit record for a given dossier, transaction, or signature — including all state changes, validation results, sign-offs, and transmissions — suitable for Health Canada inspection or third-party audit, without permitting redaction of the underlying immutable trail.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN an inspection request for a dossier WHEN export is run THEN the system produces a complete, time-ordered, human-readable audit report covering authoring, validation, sign-off, and transmission events
GIVEN an exported audit report WHEN compared to the live immutable trail THEN no events are omitted or altered
GIVEN an audit export WHEN generated THEN the export action itself is recorded in the audit trail with actor and timestamp
functional.rationale: NFR-002 mandates an immutable trail but nothing makes it inspector-consumable; an HC inspection or audit demands an on-demand, complete, readable export of that trail.
functional.traces_to: GAP: inspection-ready audit export beyond NFR-002 internal trail

nonfunctional.statement: The system SHALL define and meet documented availability, recovery point (RPO) and recovery time (RTO) objectives for all submission, sequence, acknowledgement, audit, and signature data, with backups and failover confined to in-Canada Protected B regions and periodically restore-tested.
nonfunctional.target: Documented RPO/RTO met in DR tests; backups/failover 100% in-Canada; periodic tested restoration with integrity verification

nonfunctional.statement: The system SHALL apply graceful degradation and integrity-preserving error handling so that failures in external dependencies (FDA ESG, REP ID issuance, acknowledgement ingestion, schema validators) never corrupt, partially write, or silently discard dossier/sequence state, and every such failure is logged to the audit trail.
nonfunctional.target: Zero partial-write/state-corruption on external-dependency failure; all failures audit-logged with retry/resume offered

nonfunctional.statement: The system SHALL enforce configurable data-retention schedules and legal-hold for all regulated records (submissions, sequences, acknowledgements, audit trails, signature manifests) meeting or exceeding HC/PIPEDA minimums, preventing deletion within retention or under hold and logging all disposition events.
nonfunctional.target: No deletion within retention window or under legal hold; all disposition events immutably logged; retention periods configurable as data

nonfunctional.statement: The system SHALL serialize and isolate concurrent operations so that simultaneous multi-user authoring and sequence creation within a dossier cannot produce lost updates, duplicate sequence numbers, or inconsistent backbones, under expected concurrent-user load.
nonfunctional.target: Zero lost updates or duplicate sequence-number assignments under concurrent multi-user load

nonfunctional.statement: The system SHALL be subject to documented computerized-system validation (IQ/OQ/PQ) and formal change control such that every production code or configuration change affecting backbone generation, validation rules, checksums, or e-signatures is validated, version-controlled, and traceable to an approved change record before release.
nonfunctional.target: 100% of GxP-impacting changes covered by an approved, traceable change record with IQ/OQ/PQ evidence before production

nonfunctional.statement: The system SHALL provide a Test/pre-production environment that uses synthetic or de-identified data and is isolated from Production submission/health data, so that ESG test round-trips, ruleset upgrades, and feature validation never expose or commingle real Protected B data.
nonfunctional.target: No real Protected B data in non-production; full logical and credential isolation between Test and Production

metrics.name: Submission preparation cycle time (intake to transmit-ready)
metrics.baseline: Manual/legacy: ~15-30 business days per ANDS sequence from intake to a CESG-ready package. Fragmented authoring -> hand-off to a publishing specialist -> manual bookmarking/hyperlinking -> backbone build in a desktop publisher -> terminal validation -> rework loops. Initial 0000 sequences and deficiency-response sequences skew to the high end.
metrics.target: <= 5 business days median for a standard BE-based ANDS sequence (>=60% reduction). Continuous inline validation (REQ-023), ANDS auto-gating (REQ-004), single-entry REP metadata (REQ-043), and automated bookmarking/hyperlinking (REQ-011/012) collapse the author->publish->validate chain into one workflow.
metrics.measured_by: Timestamp delta in the audit trail (NFR-002) between submission-intake creation and the transaction reaching 'transmittable' (all Errors cleared, QA review + e-signature gate passed per REQ-039). Reported as median and p90 per sequence type (initial vs response vs administrative), excluding sponsor-side content-authoring wait time (clock-stop on 'awaiting content').

metrics.name: eCTD validation error rate (Error-severity findings at build)
metrics.baseline: Manual/legacy: typically 5-20 Error-severity findings discovered at the terminal validation gate per sequence (broken bookmarks/links, checksum mismatch, naming/path-length, empty folders, sequence gaps, M1 metadata), each requiring a republish cycle. Many surface only after the package is assembled.
metrics.target: 0 Error-severity findings remaining at the point of transmit, with >=95% of all Errors caught and surfaced inline during authoring (not at the terminal gate). Warnings allowed with advisories.
metrics.measured_by: Pre-submission validation report (REQ-024) run against pinned ruleset v5.3 (REQ-022): count of Error-severity findings at transmit-ready must equal 0 (hard gate). Separately, ratio of Errors first surfaced inline during authoring vs only at the final report, computed from validation-event timestamps in the audit trail.

metrics.name: First-pass technical acceptance by Health Canada (clean on first receipt)
metrics.baseline: Manual/legacy: estimated 60-80% of transactions pass HC automated validation on first receipt; the remainder draw an emailed eCTD Validation Report and must be re-filed as a corrected sequence. Many orgs lack reliable measurement of this at all.
metrics.target: >= 98% of transmitted sequences receive a Health Canada Acknowledgement Receipt with zero Error-severity findings on first transmission ('first-pass-clean by construction').
metrics.measured_by: Of transactions reaching HC_ACK_RECEIPT state (REQ-028), the fraction whose ingested eCTD Validation Report (REQ-029) contains zero Error-severity findings, over transmitted sequences in the period. Numerator/denominator both derived from the acknowledgement state machine and the parsed validation-report PDFs.

metrics.name: Rework / deficiency-driven re-filing rate
metrics.baseline: Manual/legacy: ~20-40% of sequences require an unplanned corrective/re-filed sequence due to technical (validation) rejection; technical rejections and content-level screening deficiencies are not cleanly separated, inflating perceived rework.
metrics.target: <= 2% technical re-filing rate (sequences re-filed to fix a validation Error HC rejected). Screening/review content deficiencies (clarifax/SDN/NOD) tracked separately and not counted as portal-attributable rework.
metrics.measured_by: Count of sequences whose immediate predecessor for the same dossier was a technical rejection (HC validation report with Errors), divided by total transmitted sequences. Linked via dossier-scoped sequence lineage and rejection-report ingestion (REQ-029, REQ-047). Content-deficiency responses (REQ-032) excluded from this metric and reported on a separate deficiency-rate line.

metrics.name: Compliance / audit readiness (inspection-ready posture)
metrics.baseline: Manual/legacy: audit trails fragmented across desktop tools, file shares, and email; assembling an inspection package takes days to weeks of manual collation; e-signatures often not bound to specific signed bytes; data-residency and breach posture frequently undocumented.
metrics.target: On-demand, complete, time-ordered audit export for any dossier/transaction/signature produced in minutes; 100% of Protected B data resident in Canada; tamper-evident append-only trail disable-able by no role; every e-signature bound to the signed artifact's checksum.
metrics.measured_by: (a) Time to produce a complete inspection-ready audit export (REQ-060) - target minutes, measured by export job duration; (b) automated conformance checks: audit trail un-disableable (NFR-002), in-Canada residency 100% (NFR-001), e-signature manifest binds artifact+checksum for 100% of signed transactions (REQ-053); (c) CSV/change-control coverage of GxP-impacting changes = 100% (NFR-020). Pass/fail per control with the audit export as evidence.

metrics.name: Traceability (identifier and cross-artifact consistency; lifecycle integrity)
metrics.baseline: Manual/legacy: REP identifiers re-keyed across CO/RT/PI, cover letter, and backbone -> mismatch errors; multi-sequence lifecycle tracked in spreadsheets -> dangling prior-leaf references and gapped sequences; no reliable 'current view' of live leaves.
metrics.target: 0 identifier-mismatch defects across CO/RT/PI/cover-letter/ca-regional.xml; 0 dangling prior-leaf references and 0 sequence gaps in emitted backbones; deterministic 'current view' reconstruction available for every dossier.
metrics.measured_by: Cross-artifact consistency validator (REQ-059) and identifier format/binding checks (REQ-042/043) report 0 Errors at transmit; lifecycle validator (REQ-016/017/018) confirms gapless 4-digit numbering and every replace/append/delete resolves to a live prior leaf within the same dossier (REQ-047). Measured as defect counts in the pre-submission report plus a backbone-integrity assertion (no unresolved leaf references).

metrics.name: RA-associate effort / hours per sequence
metrics.baseline: Manual/legacy: ~20-40 person-hours per ANDS sequence, including a dedicated publishing specialist for backbone build, manual bookmarking/hyperlinking, manual checksum/path checks, and rework iterations. Requires scripting/publishing expertise and significant training.
metrics.target: <= 8 person-hours per standard sequence (>=60% reduction) and zero dependence on a separate publishing specialist or scripting; RA Associate completes authoring-through-transmit unaided via the guided UI (NFR-011).
metrics.measured_by: Active working-time per sequence attributed to RA roles, from session/audit activity timestamps (time-on-task across authoring, validation-fix, and transmission events), excluding idle and clock-stop intervals. Reported per role; complemented by a controlled time-and-motion comparison (same ANDS built legacy vs portal) for the build-acceptance milestone.

success_criteria: End-to-end ANDS happy path works: a new sponsor org can complete onboarding (CO XML with preserved immutable filename + 5-digit Company ID per REQ-001; Dossier ID request with 8-week gate and ^m[0-9]{6}$ validation per REQ-002; FDA ESG setup with mandatory Test round-trip gating Production per REQ-003/NFR-012), create an ANDS that auto-suppresses Module 4 and (on CS-BE) Modules 2.4-2.7 (REQ-004), author Module 3 CMC + BE in 5.3.1.2, pass the validation gate with 0 Errors, QA-sign (REQ-039), and reach HC_ACK_RECEIPT.

Deterministic dual-backbone correctness: index.xml + index-md5.txt at sequence root and m1/ca/ca-regional.xml (Canadian Module 1 Schema v2.2) are generated, schema/DTD-valid, and byte-identical across repeated runs on identical content (REQ-014, NFR-014). Per-leaf MD5 is computed, recorded with checksum-type 'MD5', and re-verified against actual bytes with a hard block on any mismatch (REQ-015). Automated test asserts byte-equality and tampered-file detection.

Validation engine is data-driven and complete: ruleset modeled as {rule_id, category, severity, description, ruleset_version}, default v5.3, version-selectable without code changes (REQ-022, REQ-040, NFR-013). Hard-block rules verified by test fixtures that each trigger and clear: empty folder A01, file >=200 MB A03a/b, invalid/duplicate backbone A06a/H08, checksum mismatch, sequence gap A05a/A05b/A07, encrypted/corrupt A09, non-searchable PDF B49/D29, path >200 chars B08, naming/leaf-ID B32/B47/B48, controlled-vocabulary I08. Any Error blocks transmit; Warnings advise only.

Continuous inline validation: a defect introduced during authoring appears in the severity-colored gutter mapped to the exact file/node within the active editing session (REQ-023, NFR-008 within a few seconds), and a one-click fix applies the correction and re-validates. Demonstrated for at least bookmark, hyperlink, naming, and checksum defect classes.

Lifecycle correctness across sequences: gapless 4-digit numbering starting at 0000 (REQ-016); every replace/append/delete persists a valid prior-leaf reference and no emitted backbone contains a dangling reference (REQ-017); 'current view' reconstruction shows exactly the live leaves with originating sequence and history retained (REQ-018); file reuse re-points without re-shipping bytes while preserving checksums (REQ-019). All scoped strictly per-dossier with zero cross-dossier leakage (REQ-047).

Truthful closed-loop transmission: 10 GB ceiling enforced pre-flight with <=10 GB -> gateway and >10 GB -> physical-media workflow (REQ-025/REQ-058); one-transaction-at-a-time per-dossier queue holds the next sequence until the prior HC acknowledgement (REQ-027); the acknowledgement state machine advances SENT -> MDN_RECEIVED -> FDA_ACK -> HC_ACK_RECEIPT and shows 'received by Health Canada' ONLY on the HC Acknowledgement Receipt, never on the MDN (REQ-028); rejection ingests the emailed eCTD Validation Report PDF and maps each error back to the exact tree node (REQ-029).

Failure-mode and integrity handling: external-service failures (ESG timeout/5xx, REP unavailable, schema-validation failure) never corrupt, partially write, or silently discard sequence state; the work is retained and a guided retry/resume is offered, with every failure audit-logged (REQ-045, NFR-017). Stalled/failed transmissions (no MDN, MDN-without-ACK, transport rejection) are detected by timeout monitors and an unverified duplicate send of the same sequence is prevented without explicit confirmation + recorded rationale (REQ-046).

Compliance spine enforced: Protected B data 100% resident in Canada with no cross-border replication (NFR-001); always-on tamper-evident append-only audit trail no role (including super-admin) can disable or edit, capturing actor/timestamp+timezone/action/before-after/version (NFR-002); ALCOA+ e-signatures re-authenticate at signing and bind identity+timestamp+meaning, with a signature manifest binding the signed artifact checksum and invalidating on post-sign modification (NFR-003, REQ-053); multi-tenant RBAC with hard tenant isolation proven by a cross-tenant access-denied + audit-logged test (REQ-038, NFR-015); PIPEDA breach log immutable >=24 months (NFR-006); configurable retention + legal hold blocking deletion (REQ-054/NFR-018).

ANDS-native domain logic correct: CRP capture requires brand/DIN/strength/dosage-form/manufacturer with a foreign-CRP justification path and pharmaceutical-equivalence check (REQ-007); CS-BE builder emits the 2.7.1 summary, links pivotal reports into 5.3.1.2, and flags AUC 90% CI outside 80.00-125.00% and Cmax outside configured limits (REQ-008); tree placement and required-document checklist (incl. .docx-alongside-PDF) are driven by HC's 2024-04-02 placement table as versioned data (REQ-009, REQ-044).

v4.0 readiness without re-platform: the backbone generator sits behind a version-pluggable interface, persistent document UUIDs are assigned now and retained across sequences, and the same content model can be wired to emit an HL7-RPS v4.0 message later without re-authoring content (REQ-041). Demonstrated by an interface seam plus a stub/secondary generator test.

Ruleset/schema version-transition safety: a sequence accepted under v5.3 is pinned to v5.3 and is never retroactively failed when a later ruleset activates; an in-progress dossier that crosses an effective-date boundary is warned and offered re-validation; lifecycle references remain valid across a schema-version boundary (REQ-056).

Concurrency safety: simultaneous multi-user authoring and next-sequence creation within one dossier cannot produce lost updates or duplicate sequence numbers; sequence-number assignment is serialized so exactly one user obtains the next 4-digit number under contention, and idle locks release safely (REQ-057, NFR-019). Verified by a concurrent-load test.

Test coverage and CSV evidence: automated tests exist and pass for every MUST functional requirement and every hard-block validation rule, the deterministic-backbone byte-equality assertion, the acknowledgement state machine (including MDN-is-not-receipt), tenant-isolation denial, and the e-signature tamper-detection path; all GxP-impacting changes (backbone generation, validation rules, checksums, e-signatures) are traceable to an approved change record with IQ/OQ/PQ evidence (NFR-020).

Disaster recovery proven: a documented RPO/RTO is defined and met in a tested restoration of dossiers, sequences, acknowledgements, audit trails, and signature manifests, with backups confined to in-Canada Protected B regions and restoration integrity verified against checksums (REQ-055, NFR-016).
